issues.legal_issue: A single failure to pay rent when due, without sufficient cause, constitutes a failure to pay rent regularly and may support a tenant’s ejectment.
material_facts: The tenants failed to pay rent for their holdings by the due date.
The tenants did not show sufficient cause for the non-payment.

The landlord sought ejectment on the basis of the rent default; the revenue authorities ordered ejectment, but the High Court set those orders aside on the view that a single default was insufficient.
issues.conclusion: A single default in paying rent, if made without sufficient cause, constitutes a failure to pay rent regularly and makes the tenant liable to ejectment. The appeals were allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the Collector’s ejectment orders were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1)(ii) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953 treats a failure to pay rent regularly without sufficient cause as a ground for ejectment. “Regularly” means punctually and consistently, without a break or breach; the phrase “without sufficient cause” permits a default, whether single or repeated, to be excused only if sufficient cause is shown. The Explanation to section 9(1), addressing arrears for clause (iii), supported the interpretation because it expressly provided a period for curing arrears there but did not provide that a single default under clause (ii) could be condoned. The Court relied on Arab Bank Ltd. v. Ross and Hammond v. London County Council for the meaning of “regular,” and referred to Bhagirath Ram Chand v. State of Punjab concerning the Act’s purpose. It also applied the principle that courts must give effect to the plain statutory language and should not add an exception the legislature did not provide.

rule.if: tenant_ejectment_proceeding and rent_was_not_paid_punctually and not sufficient_cause_shown

predicates.tenant_ejectment_proceeding: The proceeding was brought to seek a tenant’s ejectment from rented land.
predicates.rent_was_not_paid_punctually: The tenant failed to pay rent when it was due, creating at least one break in punctual payment.
predicates.sufficient_cause_shown: The tenant showed sufficient cause for the failure to pay rent.

issues.definition: If an ejectment proceeding concerns a tenant who failed to pay rent punctually and did not show sufficient cause, the tenant is liable to ejectment.
